question_text_max300: Does the heterozygote show a measurable partial deficit (Tc-MEP onset latency 2.13 against 1.39 ms in wild type, null 2.44; amplitude normal; Cheng 2020, 3 weeks, n = 5) that could serve as a carrier readout, and does it replicate?
decision_at_stake_max200: Whether a heterozygote conduction readout can enter the carrier premise of the pup brief and the myelin cards.
status_evidence: [IT 2026-11-19, ADV-075, audit G row 1 confirmed against the original and CORRECTED] Cheng 2020 (PMC text, Results 'Nerve degeneration and demyelination', Fig 2): Tc-MEP at 3 weeks, wild type amplitude 59.2 ± 9.0 uV, latency 1.39 ± 0.13 ms (n = 10); heterozygote 59.6 ± 17.2 uV, 2.13 ± 0.22 ms (n = 5; latency P < 0.05 against wild type; paper: 'partial Tc-MEP deteriorative change'); null 11.8 ± 5.4 uV, 2.44 ± 0.37 ms (n = 4); one-way ANOVA generally, no named post hoc test, no heterozygote against null comparison, the legend says SEM. The audit's statement that the heterozygote latency 'equals the null' is NOT in the source (2.13 against 2.44 ms; the paper calls it partial); its 'amplitude normal' is right. Carried before: the amplitude values only, in the IT56-Q02 origin table (measurements.tsv, a work folder, not a need, card or arm cell); the latency was carried nowhere. Limits: one laboratory, small n, n for the latency panel not given separately, anaesthetised (chloral hydrate), 3 weeks only. Dated 2026-11-19 (IT, ADV-077): entry for a laboratory: row 10 (heterozygote carrier latency) of SCI's ordering page, experiment_brief_presidio013_sci_20261116/v2_consolidated_sci_20261119/ORDERING_PAGE.md.
blocking_reason: Needs a laboratory with heterozygote and null animals and Tc-MEP or an equivalent conduction readout.

(glucose in the S-KO and N-KO lines, glucose with same-animal EEG/ECoG from P9, a restoration arm without WWOX restoration, ketone, lactate, insulin by age)
decision_at_stake_max200: Whether a glucose measurement series enters the pup design (optional, tied to seizure timing); the metabolic lever stays out of the comparison set.
status_evidence: [IT 2026-11-19, mapped from SCI's ADV-074 first pass, note advisor_pilot_20261113/brainstorm_20261116/h_glucose_axis_adv074_sci_20261119/GLUCOSE_METABOLIC_AXIS_FIRST_PASS_ADV074_SCI_20261119.md and R4 report as delivered] SCI's wording in full: 'Does hypoglycaemia or another metabolic state drive excitability, seizures and death in the Wwox-null pup, or only accompany them? Separating measurements: glucose in the S-KO and N-KO seizure-and-death lines (never reported), glucose at seizure time with same-animal EEG/ECoG from P9, a glucose-restoration arm without WWOX restoration, ketone/lactate/insulin by age and milk intake (none measured in any held original).' The held originals cannot answer it: no original manipulates glucose; the neuronal rescues normalise glucose, growth, seizures and survival together (a central origin of the hypoglycaemia, not glucose as the cause of seizures); no glucose before P10 although the neuron-targeted deletion seizes from P9; no glucose at the time of any seizure; ECoG starts at P14. Access: the lde/lde rat original is not held or recoverable (the receipt cites two absent files). Stop rule as written by ADV is not met (age-resolved glucose beyond P10 exists, the link to seizure timing does not): the axis is not closed. Dated 2026-11-19 (IT, ADV-077): entry for a laboratory: row 7 (glucose tied to seizure timing) of SCI's ordering page, experiment_brief_presidio013_sci_20261116/v2_consolidated_sci_20261119/ORDERING_PAGE.md.
blocking_reason: Needs a laboratory with the seizure-and-death lines and same-animal glucose and EEG or ECoG; the rat original needs a supply path.
